analysis.title: 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (31st Annual Edition): Productivity returns: An investment surge lifts growth ... and volatility
key_insights: The 10 to 15 year outlook is built on three themes: economic nationalism, technology adoption (mainly AI) and capital rewiring. A USD 15 trillion global capex boom centered on technology adoption is expected to lift growth and asset returns, with higher inflation volatility.
G7 nominal growth is raised 30bps to 4.2%, the best in 15 years. Global real GDP is 2.6% (2.5% last year) and global inflation is unchanged at 2.6%. Developed market growth is 1.9% (1.7% last year).

U.S. long-term real GDP growth is raised to 2.1% from 1.8%, driven almost entirely by AI. AI adds about 40bps to U.S. total factor productivity (TFP) growth, taking it to 1.2%, and about 30bps to capital stock growth, taking it to 2.3%. Labor productivity rises 50bps to 2.2%.

A balanced 60/40 global stock-bond portfolio in USD is forecast at 7.0%, up 60bps from 6.4% last year. Adding 30% diversified alternatives lifts the forecast to 7.5% and the Sharpe ratio 21% above a public-markets-only portfolio.

U.S. large cap equity forecast rises 80bps to 7.5%, the highest since the pandemic, on a terminal margin assumption of 15.1% and higher revenue growth. Global equity (ACWI) rises 50bps to 7.5%. The U.S. vs rest-of-world return gap moves from -70bps to +10bps.

For the first time in the publication's history, developed market equity forecasts sit above emerging market forecasts. Korea and Taiwan are 51% of the EM index and are dominated by cyclical chipmakers, so their current supernormal margins are expected to normalize, which drags EM returns (7.1% USD).

Global bond return forecasts are the highest in two decades. USD 10-year bonds are 5.5% and 30-year bonds 6.2%, investment grade credit 6.1% and high yield 6.7%. Drivers are higher starting yields, normalized real yields, steeper curves and rebuilt term premia. The firm still sees duration as a less reliable hedge when inflation uncertainty is high.

Credit views diverge by sector. High yield is upgraded on better index quality (higher BB share). Investment grade cycle-neutral spreads are cut 20bps because heavy hyperscaler issuance raises index quality. Leveraged loans get higher default and spread assumptions, with about 30% of defaults and distressed deals now involving repeat liability-management borrowers.

The trade-weighted dollar is still seen as structurally overvalued and set for slower depreciation, concentrated against Asian currencies (KRW, JPY, CNY). European crosses are closer to fair value. The dollar's reserve status is not seen as challenged.

Bitcoin gets a long-term return range for the first time but is excluded from the main covariance matrices. The 10-year annualized forecast is a 10.0% base case, -11.2% bear and 16.6% bull. The authors call BTC a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing, and say it is premature to treat it as a portfolio diversifier because its correlations are unstable.

Alternatives forecasts are raised broadly. Diversified hedge funds rise 140bps to 6.7% on higher carry on shorts, better alpha and methodology changes. Global core real estate is 7.9%, global infrastructure 7.1%, global transport 8.1% (up from 7.9%) and commodities 4.8%. Gold is unchanged at 5.5%. Large cap private equity falls 60bps to 9.6% on financing costs. Return dispersion across managers is expected to widen.

Volatility and correlation assumptions are raised. Equity volatility rises, especially U.S., which keeps Sharpe ratios roughly unchanged. The stock-bond correlation is projected at a positive 0.34 and is unstable. Inflation shocks are expected nearly twice as often as historically, with a 12.5% weight on high inflation and rate uncertainty regimes.

Portfolio guidance: keep U.S. equities but diversify regionally, with Europe and Japan as diversification options. Use inflation-linked bonds, gold, real assets and liquid alternatives against supply shocks, and keep duration for demand shocks. Reduce tech-adoption exposure by cutting U.S. and EM equity and long-duration bonds and adding developed ex-U.S. equity, core real estate and gold.

Climate chapter: climate damage hits the stock of wealth rather than GDP flow, so it should show up as supply shocks, inflation volatility and higher term premia rather than a smooth growth drag. Relative winners include adaptation suppliers, critical mineral processors, regulated utilities and reinsurers with pricing power.

Main risks are mismeasuring the balance between capital and labor in the K-shaped economy, restrictions on capital flows, AI capex that fails to lift productivity, fiscal and central bank independence erosion, and geopolitical fragmentation. Upside risks include a broader AI productivity boom and faster energy transition.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A 30bps upgrade driven almost entirely by AI-led productivity and capital deepening.
Highest in 15 years with the best real growth to inflation mix since the pandemic.
Modest upgrade from AI and capex in developed markets and selected emerging markets, offsetting demographic drags.
Average inflation stays tame but with more frequent and larger bouts of volatility.
Modestly lowered as trade and supply shocks fade, while euro area (2.2%) and Japan (1.9%) are raised.
20bps AI TFP upgrade plus higher capital services growth from defense and grid investment.

macro_indicators.indicator: U.S. stock-bond correlation (global equity vs U.S. Aggregate)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Positive, drifting higher and unstable, which weakens duration as a diversifier in supply shocks.
Improved but still below the 3% of the internet era, and the report says the gain may reflect supply-side shocks more than AI.

crypto_views: JPM initiates a 10-year bitcoin return range: base 10.0%, bear -11.2%, bull 16.6% annualized from a spot of USD 83,000. The overall figure weights three frameworks 65:30:5 (supply growth vs global money supply, complement to gold, network adoption).
BTC is not added to the main covariance matrices. A standalone matrix shows 55.0% volatility, 20.9% arithmetic return and correlation of 0.33 with U.S. large cap and 0.10 with gold.

BTC is seen as a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing that mostly trades like a high-beta risk asset tracking global money supply. It is not yet a strategic diversifier because of unstable correlations and very high volatility.

Crypto is an asset class worth over USD 2.5 trillion. Tokenized assets such as money market funds are around USD 40 billion. About a tenth of surveyed family office clients held crypto and 17% planned to prioritize crypto and digital assets.
Conditions for a larger role: lower volatility, stable correlations, clearer regulation, deeper liquidity and better price discovery.
risk_factors: Miscalculating the balance between the upper and lower legs of the K-shaped economy, either underpaying labor or over-redistributing from capital.
Restrictions on capital flows, which economic nationalism has so far left largely untouched.
Widespread capital misallocation. If the AI investment boom fails to lift productivity, the result is lower trend growth and excess capacity that raises disinflation risk.
Hyperscaler depreciation weighing on earnings if AI revenue arrives later than planned or equipment becomes obsolete faster than the four-year assumption.
U.S. fiscal and institutional erosion, which could raise term premia, fatten the inflation tail and weaken the safe-asset premium.
Government debt markets becoming unruly so that term premia keep rising past what equity valuations can absorb.
Power scarcity from AI and data centers, with a near-term CPI and margin squeeze.
Valuations that offer little cushion, and capex cycles that often take a volatile final turn.
Weaker private credit vintages with permissive documentation and yield-chasing, and rising liquidity mismatch risk in semiliquid vehicles.
Extreme weather stressing supply chains and agricultural output, lifting prices.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 (equity return forecasts 2026 vs 2027): USD total return forecasts of 7.5% for U.S. large cap (from 6.7%), 7.7% for EAFE and 7.1% for emerging markets, with emerging markets below developed markets for the first time.
Exhibit 4B (projected stock-bond correlations by publication year): the 2027 forecast is 0.34 for global equity vs U.S. Aggregate, raised steadily since the 2023 LTCMAs.
Exhibit A (bitcoin 10-year return scenarios): overall base 10.0%, bear -11.2%, bull 16.6%, with a network adoption framework alone giving a -3.2% base case.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility forecasts are raised, notably for equities and especially U.S. equities, given valuations and capital misallocation risk. Sharpe ratios are roughly unchanged for global equity.
Long U.S. Treasury volatility is now above its post-GFC average and inflation volatility forecasts remain elevated.
Stock-bond correlation is projected at 0.34 and may drift higher. It can turn negative in demand shocks and quite positive in supply shocks.
The USD to U.S. stocks correlation, negative for 15 years, may be changing or proving more unstable, as it was in 2025.
Global equity manager and stock return dispersion is high despite an economic expansion, which the authors read as an early effect of the three themes.
Shocks tied to AI turbulence were seen in January 2025 and July 2026. A 2026 sell-off in software and semiconductor stocks may be a harbinger of more volatility.

Hedging guidance: add inflation-linked bonds, gold, real assets and liquid alternatives against supply shocks, keep duration against demand shocks, and avoid too much concentration in momentum strategies. Non-USD investors in U.S. stocks should consider hedging more of the exposure.
geopolitical: Economic nationalism: industrial strategy, tariffs and restrictions on trade and migration, with trade protectionism flagged as a risk to growth and inflation.
Deeper U.S.-China split and protracted conflicts hardwiring trade, tech and finance frictions.
Two armed conflicts in four years, in Ukraine and the Gulf, have roiled energy markets and underscored the value of energy independence.
Supply chains being weaponized and uncertainty about the reliability of traditional allies are pushing governments to bring defense, energy, critical minerals and technology in-house.
Restrictive U.S. immigration policy and export controls on advanced U.S. chips to China.
Taiwan and Korea's central role in tech supply chains is both a strength and a risk as the U.S. and China push toward onshore alternatives.

tension_points.bull_case: A historic USD 15 trillion investment boom lifts U.S. TFP by about 40bps and capital growth by about 30bps. U.S. RoIC averages around 17% over the last decade, AI adoption is tracking three times faster than the internet, and the biggest spenders have healthier fundamentals.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex may overshoot near-term monetization, with a reset in investment, equity de-rating in tech and pockets of AI supply chain credit stress. Hyperscaler depreciation weighs on earnings, and capex cycles often take a volatile final turn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the investment boom fails to boost productivity, or AI reaches only a quarter of tasks by 2040 with annual TFP growth below 1%, the forecast upgrades would be too high.

tension_points.bull_case: A rising productivity tide lifts enough boats to avoid the most reactionary policies, so the metastable K-shaped economy persists and keeps channeling reward to capital to sustain growth and profits.
tension_points.bear_case: If the lower leg of the K is not rewarded enough to sustain the social contract, economic nationalism accelerates. Over-redistribution from capital to labor could disincentivize investment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Factors that push the balance of rewards between capital and labor too far in either direction would break the metastable equilibrium and cause bouts of volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Clearer regulation, ETFs, futures, custody and deeper liquidity are improving the asset. Fiat debasement and supply growth underpin a 10.0% base case and 16.6% bull case 10-year return.
tension_points.bear_case: Unstable correlations and 55% volatility prevent a strategic role. The bear case is -11.2% annualized and BTC fundamentals are not cash flows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If volatility keeps declining and correlations to other assets stabilize, BTC's portfolio utility may improve.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI adoption and capital deepening lift trend growth, margins and equity returns over 10 to 15 years, especially in the U.S.
theme_stances.evidence: technology adoption is the fair wind filling its sails

theme_stances.key_argument: Resilient U.S. margins and RoIC beat cyclical-tech-heavy EM margins in Korea and Taiwan, which are expected to normalize.
theme_stances.evidence: for the first time, our DM equity forecasts sit above those for EM equities

theme_stances.key_argument: Normalized real yields, steeper curves and higher starting yields lift bond forecasts, though duration is a less reliable hedge.
theme_stances.evidence: global sovereign bonds offering the best return forecasts in two decades

theme_stances.key_argument: Unstable correlations and high volatility keep BTC from a strategic diversifier role for now.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not make a case for bitcoin (BTC) as a diversifier in portfolios
